summary: Third fleet vertical slice: wire bounded leases (TTL) and per-round renew heartbeat into the real SubAgentRunner lifecycle, expose the coordinator's recover() disk facts (expires_at/expired/settlement) through a read-only subagent_lease tool surface, and close the silent-workspace-creation hazard in recover()/reclaim_run_if_expired() (read-only lookups now fail honestly on unknown run keys).

components.owning_subsystem: fleet workspace/lease lifecycle owned by ProjectCoordinator/FleetStore (fleet state.json); runner-side heartbeat is a lifecycle fact, not a new authority
components.disposition: ADMIT. TTL and renew reuse slice-2 primitives; the runner passes ttl_seconds at begin_run and renews once per child round while genuinely alive. Renew failure is fail-soft: the authority boundary stays the fence at settlement, never a mid-run kill. The new subagent_lease tool is read-only projection of recover() facts; recover()/reclaim_run_if_expired() switch to a read-only workspace lookup (KeyError on unknown run key) so observation no longer mutates fleet state. No model-semantic judgment is added.
evidence: RED first: test_fleet_runner_renew_and_tool.py collected with ModuleNotFoundError for tools.builtin.subagent_lease and TypeError for missing fleet_lease_ttl_seconds kwarg before implementation.
Round-boundary renew strictly extends expires_at (monotonic) in a real two-round child run; settled lease retains expires_at.
Rival reclaim mid-run: child completes, fenced settle yields zero settlements, superseded(gen1)/active(gen2) rows visible on disk.
Crashed child with ttl=0.15s: after real 0.25s sleep, subagent_lease reports expired=true state=active expires_at present.
recover('never-begun-run') now raises KeyError and leaves workspaces empty (no silent creation).
components.verification_level: RED-first focused TDD (7 tests), adjacent fleet/subagent suites, full pytest (not real_llm), Ruff, Pyright, A.5 self-gate
components.model_evidence_veto_recovery_exit: subagent_lease only reports mechanical facts (expired=true is a lease-expiry fact, not a takeover instruction); ttl=None on SubAgentRunner preserves the previous never-expire behavior explicitly; operators can revert the single commit without any fleet-state migration.
components.rollback_route: Revert this commit; no fleet state.json migration is required (expires_at is an additive optional field).

g1.necessity: Slice-2 introduced TTL primitives, but the real SubAgentRunner lifecycle never passed a ttl and never renewed: leases were unbounded in practice, a crashed child left an immortal active lease, and no model-facing surface exposed expires_at/expired, so time-licensed takeover had no observable facts and no honest unknown-key behavior (recover silently created workspace state).

g2.authority_owner: FleetStore state.json under the existing ProjectCoordinator project scope
g2.non_duplication: No new store, controller, scheduler, or verdict mechanism. begin_run/renew_run/settle fencing are reused as-is; the runner only supplies ttl_seconds and a per-round heartbeat call. subagent_lease is a read-only projection of recover(); recover()/reclaim_run_if_expired() reuse the same store through a new find_workspace read path instead of get_or_create.

model_evidence: subagent_lease tool reports workspace_id, lease generation/worker/owner/state, expires_at, expired, and settlement outcome straight from disk
runner logs a warning on renew failure with the exact exception type
tests show expired=true after real clock expiry on a crashed child and settled outcome=completed on a healthy child
g3.recovery_or_reason: fleet_lease_ttl_seconds=None keeps the previous never-expire behavior as an explicit exit; fenced renew/settle never kills a live child loop; reverting the single commit removes the wiring with no data migration.

g4.rollback: Revert the single commit; expires_at is an additive optional field in lease rows and no migration of existing fleet state is required.
